prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Inside a small tent, the depth map grades the scene from the bright foreground pouch and the camera wearer's hands at the lower center (about 0.3–0.5 m away, within arm's reach) and the curved right-side tent wall (0.3–0.6 m) to a bundled blue sleeping bag or jacket in the middle ground (0.7–1.2 m) and a dark backpack behind it on the upper left (1.2–1.5 m). Across frames 1 to 4, the camera wearer's left hand reaches forward from the bottom-left toward a person sitting on the left (~0.8–1.0 m away, about 0.3 m left of the sleeping bag), and in frame 5 the camera pans up and left as that person leans in to hand over a bright white pouch at ~0.4–0.8 m while pushing the sleeping bag and backpack to the lower right. The person on the left is largely cropped out at the left edge in frames 1–4 and becomes more visible in frame 5, facing downward and slightly right rather than looking directly at the camera wearer, while the foreground pouch is partly cropped at the bottom edge. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map more clearly separates the curved 3D contour of the right tent flap, the raised hood of the blue sleeping bag, and the recessed background backpack behind it. However, it is unreliable on the white upper tent wall, rendering that nearby fabric (~1.5 m away) completely black as if at infinite distance and merging the dark backpack into the background in frame 3.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map outlines the large central mound of the blue sleeping bag and surrounding red/yellow pads (~0.5–1.2 m in front of the camera wearer), a dark bag behind it to the upper left (~1.2–1.5 m away), the small open pouch in the lower-center foreground (~0.3–0.5 m away), and the person positioned on the left (~0.6–1.0 m away, adjacent to the sleeping bag). Across frames 1 to 4, the person on the left enters the left edge within arm's reach of both the sleeping bag and the camera wearer's extended hand, and in frame 5 a single pink 'person' mask captures their upper body leaning down from the upper left while holding a green-masked object ('remote', ~0.4 m away) at the bottom center as the camera turns left. Whereas the RGB image shows complex overlapping fabrics, the segmentation map isolates distinct object boundaries in frame 3—separating the rear bag ('suitcase'), the person's arm ('person') and leg on the left, and the main sleeping bag mound—and tracks the small handheld object moving from left to bottom center in frames 4 and 5. However, the map is highly unreliable in class labeling and temporal consistency: it misclassifies the motionless sleeping bag mound as a 'person', labels the foreground pouch as 'banana' in frame 1 and 'remote' in frame 2 before dropping it in frames 3–5, and switches the rear backpack from 'backpack' (frame 2) to 'suitcase' (frame 3) to unsegmented background (frames 4–5). It also omits the tent walls entirely and completely misses the sleeping bag and background bag in frame 5 when they shift into the lower-right corner.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks skeletal keypoints inside the tent, detecting only the camera wearer's magenta left hand at the bottom-left (~0.3 m away, within arm's reach of the foreground pouch) in frame 1, nothing in frame 2, mistaken yellow body skeletons on the blue sleeping bag mound (~0.7–1.2 m in front) in frames 3 and 4, and the actual person on the left (~0.6–0.8 m away) in frame 5. In frame 5, the yellow torso rectangle and left-arm keypoints show the person on the upper left leaning forward and downward toward the lower center, with facial keypoints clustered at the top-left edge indicating their head is turned down and slightly right rather than looking at the camera wearer. While the person's lower body and right arm are occluded or out of frame on the left and the sleeping bag is pushed to the lower right in frame 5, the pose map clearly reveals the exact shoulder-torso-wrist geometry and head orientation of the darkly clothed person against the dark jacket in frame 5, which is harder to discern in RGB. Conversely, the map is severely unreliable in frames 1–4: it completely misses the person sitting on the left in frames 1–4 and fails to detect the camera wearer's reaching hands in frames 2–4 and the other person's hands in frames 3–4. Furthermore, in frames 3 and 4 it hallucinates a horizontal body skeleton and facial keypoints onto the inanimate, hooded blue sleeping bag, falsely depicting a person lying face-down with a head at the right hood (~0.8 m away) and limbs extending left (~1.0 m away).
